contribution.description: Established from a live directory listing that agent/repo_requirements_audit_validate.py does not exist, so t7's validator must be created fresh rather than repaired.

pitfalls.problem: PROGRESS.json on venice/repo-hierarchical-audit-v2 described the superseded v1 task.
pitfalls.failed_approach: Reusing the previous audit's PROGRESS.json as current assignment state.
pitfalls.lesson: Rewrite PROGRESS.json for the active task id with its live blob SHA as expected_sha; confirm the new blob on the next read.

pitfalls.problem: Workflow branch filter and source-matched test referenced the v1 branch, so no green run existed on the active v2 branch.
pitfalls.failed_approach: Assuming flipping the workflow filter alone would green the suite.
pitfalls.lesson: Workflow branches filter + checkout ref AND tests/test_repo_requirements_audit.py must all reference venice/repo-hierarchical-audit-v2, and a green run on the active head is required to close it.

pitfalls.problem: build_hierarchy.py raised SystemExit on requirement R8.1 because STAGES lacked S8 and SUBSTAGES lacked the '8 Shadow and live'/OPS entry.
pitfalls.failed_approach: Assuming the v2 mapping covered all canonical rows; only R0.1-R6.2 had been verified.
pitfalls.lesson: Add S8 plus an S8.1 substage keyed on gantt_group '8 Shadow and live'/lane OPS, handle v1 'CLOSED', and verify build_matrices completes with no unmapped message.

pitfalls.problem: write_file and checkpoint returned 'Task assignment changed; refresh context before mutation' during an assignment revision.
pitfalls.failed_approach: Issuing a mutation in the same turn the assignment sha changed, using the older PROGRESS.json SHA.
pitfalls.lesson: After an assignment sha change, re-read the target blob on the live branch; the guard rejection is a repair instruction, not proof of a failed edit.

pitfalls.problem: docs/venice-audit-v1/__pycache__ is tracked even though .gitignore excludes pycache/ and *.pyc.
pitfalls.failed_approach: Relying on .gitignore alone; ignore rules do not untrack already-committed files.
pitfalls.lesson: Add git rm -r --cached docs/venice-audit-v1/__pycache__ before git add in the workflow commit step, then confirm the path is absent from list_files.

pitfalls.problem: build_hierarchy.py rewrites REQUIREMENTS.csv in place from the v1 schema to v2 columns, so a second run could parse already-converted rows.
pitfalls.failed_approach: Assuming the in-place rewrite is idempotent without checking the upstream regenerator.
pitfalls.lesson: Verified safe: build_matrices.run_extras calls build_extra.main() first, which always rewrites REQUIREMENTS.csv from its hardcoded ROWS list in the v1 schema. Keep that call order if either generator is refactored.

pitfalls.problem: Question rows cannot invent a parent stage: match_substage resolves parent_substage_id from (gantt_group, owner_lane) against a fixed SUBSTAGES table and SystemExits on anything unmapped; question_design/answer_generation are NOT_APPLICABLE outside S4/S5/S5B.
pitfalls.failed_approach: Treating the eight status dimensions as free-form columns attachable to any stage.
pitfalls.lesson: Question rows must target S4.1 for design, S5.1 for answer+verification and S5B.1 for alias only, and the generator must run after build_hierarchy so the substage table is materialised.

pitfalls.problem: The workflow generated every artifact into the runner workspace and threw it away.
pitfalls.failed_approach: Assuming a green audit run proves the artifact exists because the build step succeeded.
pitfalls.lesson: Fixed: the commit step now pushes regenerated outputs, so a green run at a head does produce file@sha artifacts; a GITHUB_TOKEN push still will not retrigger the workflow, so each edit_file push remains the trigger.

pitfalls.problem: The commit+push step has no if:always(), so the run that first carries the new workflow (52aa4bfe) died at pytest before the commit step and published nothing; a red run at a head whose tests still describe the previous workflow therefore looks identical to a broken commit script.
pitfalls.failed_approach: Editing workflow and tests in two separate commits and expecting the first run to publish.
pitfalls.lesson: Read a red run's job log before touching the commit step; expect one transitional red run per head whose tests still describe the previous workflow.

pitfalls.problem: QUESTION_INDEX.csv writes question_id as Q-<INVENTORY>-<LENS> only, so 17637 rows collapse to 3537 distinct ids and per-row uniqueness cannot be asserted; the manifest also counts 258 source ids while only 257 inventory_ids appear in rows.
pitfalls.failed_approach: Asserting global question_id uniqueness against a generator that keys ids only by inventory+lens.
pitfalls.lesson: Add a per-row discriminator to question_id (phase suffix after the Q-<SLUG(INVENTORY)>- prefix) and recompute counts['ids']/counts['questions'] from emitted rows after the loop; verified green.

pitfalls.problem: Native tool calls named read_file/edit_file return 'Tool not found' inside this turn.
pitfalls.failed_approach: Invoking read_file/edit_file as native function calls instead of bridge actions.
pitfalls.lesson: Put every GitHub request in actions[] as {tool,args} and read results next turn.
